en.content:
In the wake of the Tai Po fire, the government’s decision to allow victims to return home and retrieve belongings—multiple times within a defined three-hour window—reflects a practical balance between compassion and safety. For families, the ability to step back into familiar spaces is not merely administrative; it can be psychologically important and materially necessary. Property, documents, medications, and daily essentials are often irreplaceable, and a single trip may be too limited for people navigating stress, injuries, and the presence of investigators and responders. The message from officials appears to be that recovery should begin immediately, not only after investigations end.

At the same time, the inquiry into the fire—focusing on whether flammable materials and construction practices were properly opposed and scrutinised—reminds the public that “getting back” must not dilute the urgency of accountability. When an owners’ corporation and renovation contractor are found to have had differing views on safety measures, it becomes harder for residents to accept that tragedy was simply an accident of fate. The community will reasonably ask what safeguards failed: oversight procedures, procurement standards, enforcement of regulations, and the channels by which residents can influence renovation risks. The retrieval arrangement, therefore, should be seen as the first step of a broader recovery framework that includes transparent findings and clearer responsibilities for building management.

More broadly, the Tai Po case highlights a wider tension in Hong Kong’s built environment: convenience and redevelopment pressures often compete with the long, sometimes inconvenient discipline of fire safety. In a city of dense housing and frequent maintenance cycles, risk management depends not only on laws and inspections, but also on a culture of prevention—clear communication, documented decision-making, and enforceable requirements for materials and works. The government’s approach to disaster response can build public trust if it goes beyond procedural logistics and demonstrates that safety standards tightened or lessons learned will translate into concrete, enforceable changes for similar buildings.

Finally, it is worth insisting on the human centre of this policy. Allowing multiple return trips within a controlled timeframe can reduce hardship for survivors while still protecting the scene for investigation. If handled with dignity—clear guidance, sufficient assistance, and respectful coordination—such measures can help families reclaim control in the early phase of grief. And if the investigation subsequently shows where safety warnings were raised or ignored, the city should be prepared to convert that knowledge into practical reforms. Only then can “recovery” mean more than physical access; it must also mean learning how to prevent the next preventable tragedy.

zh.content:
香港近年「數據中心熱」幾乎成為新經濟地標：機房落地、投資湧入，口號亦常指向創科與未來。然而，真正考驗唔喺技術有冇進步，而係香港能否用好呢個進步——同時守住城市嘅公共利益，包括能源、環境同長遠承載力。當伺服器擴張速度快過社會對其用電、散熱及供電韌性嘅理解，創新就可能由「加速器」變成「風險放大器」。

數據中心帶來嘅效益唔難計：雲端服務、金融科技、內容分發、甚至本地企業做AI都需要更穩定嘅運算能力。但問題係，電力供應同排放成本究竟係咪被誠實納入決策？如果監管只停留喺效率指標、而忽略整體能耗足跡與增量排放，香港就可能陷入「裝得快、代價慢」嘅困局——短期看見機架與就業，長期卻要面對碳目標、電網壓力同社區承受力。創科本來應該係可持續嘅競爭力，唔係單靠物理堆疊硬件嘅總量遊戲。

此外，數據中心熱潮亦牽涉產業結構：香港要做亞洲創新樞紐，就必須確保本地生態鏈唔會只停留喺「場地與供電」角色。真正高價值應該包括資料治理、資訊安全、研發人才與跨域應用；否則城市只會愈做愈像「倉儲節點」，利潤分配同風險承擔都未必對本地公平。再者，當市民對隱私、運算資料去向同商業使用缺乏透明度時，「創科」就容易被誤讀為企業自我延伸，而唔係公共利益導向。

立場上，我認為香港可以、亦應該發展數據中心，但必須同時建立更嚴格、更透明、更可驗證嘅規劃框架：例如以碳強度與能耗上限作硬約束、要求散熱與能源來源披露、以及把「可持續」納入批地與擴建審批；同時促進本地研發與安全合規能力，避免城市淪為單一供電附屬。只有咁，數據中心先至可能真正成為創新的基建，而唔係未來十年先被迫「補鑊」嘅負擔。

en.topic_title: Fire victims returning home to collect belongings can make multiple trips within 3-hour slot, official says
en.topic_summary:
Survivors of the deadly Tai Po fire will be allowed to go in and out of their homes multiple times within their designated three-hour slot, a top government official has said, adding that journalists will not be permitted to tag along.



Deputy Chief Secretary for Administration Warner Cheuk Wing-hing meets the press on October 26, 2023. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. 



Deputy Chief Secretary for Administration Warner Cheuk made the comments on Sunday, a day before fire victims are set to go back to W
